key_insight: The CALPHAD-based Γ ductility metric modestly improves correlation with tensile ductility in refractory compositionally complex alloys while matching the DFT-based D-parameter in compression.
engineering_relevance: Γ could guide screening of refractory alloys for room-temperature ductility, a key barrier to deploying these materials in extreme-condition structures.
method: Combine the BCC–HCP free-energy difference with the interfacial free energy of a (110) BCC surface.
Include electronegativity-corrected lattice distortion in the Γ metric.
Compare ductility correlations and propose pairing Γ with CALPHAD-calculated oxygen solubility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better tensile-ductility correlation than the D-parameter and equally good performance in compression, but provides no dataset size or quantitative correlation statistics.
watch_item: Γ targets intrinsic ductility; combining it with oxygen solubility to capture extrinsic embrittlement remains a proposed first-order approach.
paper_title: Thermodynamic Underpinnings Affecting Compressive and Tensile Plasticity in Refractory Compositionally Complex Alloys
